title: Fragmentation: contiguous vs. paged
goal:
Measure the memory waste that Section 3.1 describes and that Section 4.3 removes. A request needs `L` KV slots, one per token. Write these functions:

- `blocks_needed(n_tokens, block_size)`: the number of blocks that hold `n_tokens` tokens.
- `contiguous_waste(lengths, max_len)`: the total slots wasted when every request reserves `max_len` slots up front.
- `paged_waste(lengths, block_size)`: the total slots wasted when each request holds only the blocks it needs.
- `paged_cost(n_tokens, block_size)`: the slots a request occupies in the paged layout.
- `admit_count(lengths, capacity, cost)`: serve requests in arrival order and count how many fit in `capacity` slots at once. `cost` is a function from a request length to the slots it reserves. Stop at the first request that doesn't fit; don't skip it to admit a later, smaller one.
hints: Use integer arithmetic for the ceiling: `-(-n // b)`, or `math.ceil(n / b)`.
When `n_tokens` is an exact multiple of `block_size`, the waste is 0. A formula such as `n // b + 1` fails there.
In `admit_count`, keep a running total. A request that fills the capacity exactly still fits, so compare with `>`, not `>=`.
The paged waste of one request is `blocks_needed * block_size - n_tokens`. It is always less than `block_size`.
